observer_contract:
# Final-post marker monitor contract v1

Use the unchanged public DUT pins in specification.md and the supplied module header.
The passive monitor additionally observes readonly trace_done:0 at every pre sample
and all post samples except the final post sample, where it is1. No extra rising
edge follows this marker. Enable finite-end checks combinationally from trace_done
and private state already updated by the final edge. The marker is evaluator
metadata, not a DUT input, truth label, reset or stimulus modification.

Development evaluations require drained=true,min_tail32; final evaluations use
drained=true,min_tail128. Definite failures and unknowns retain their independent
reference meanings; a short tail is never automatically accepted. A presented
valid safety failure is distinct from end-only response/input completion failure.
Independent reference inputs remain exactly the original six inputs/nine outputs;
the marker does not modify the Claude reference function or DUT specification.

Six active/ok slots,body<=16000UTF8bytes,state<=8192bits; readonly public pins,
posedge clk only, no hierarchy/files/assumptions/system calls. Short formal safety
projection explicitly sets trace_done=0 and cannot prove finite completion.

raw_coverage.decode: ordinary:8 columns; columns0/3/4/5/6 index strings (null stays null), column7 indexes vector of three trace hits. toggle:[site,bits,three vector IDs]; site0/3/4 index strings. bits range=[range,start,count] or list=[list,values]; vectors restore original RLE arrays. Metadata restores all other fields. Every source counter and per-trace count stays separate.

metadata.rule: For each listed bit in order, keep separate0->1 and1->0 counters. Decode run[value,count] arrays; no source counter is merged.

/*
 * AXI4-Stream frame length adjuster with FIFO
 */
module axis_frame_length_adjust_fifo #
(
    // Width of AXI stream interfaces in bits
    parameter DATA_WIDTH = 8,
    // Propagate tkeep signal
    // If disabled, tkeep assumed to be 1'b1
    parameter KEEP_ENABLE = (DATA_WIDTH>8),
    // tkeep signal width (words per cycle)
    parameter KEEP_WIDTH = ((DATA_WIDTH+7)/8),
    // Propagate tid signal
    parameter ID_ENABLE = 0,
    // tid signal width
    parameter ID_WIDTH = 8,
    // Propagate tdest signal
    parameter DEST_ENABLE = 0,
    // tdest signal width
    parameter DEST_WIDTH = 8,
    // Propagate tuser signal
    parameter USER_ENABLE = 1,
    // tuser signal width
    parameter USER_WIDTH = 1,
    // Depth of data FIFO in words
    parameter FRAME_FIFO_DEPTH = 4096,
    // Depth of header FIFO
    parameter HEADER_FIFO_DEPTH = 8
)
(
    input  wire                   clk,
    input  wire                   rst,

    /*
     * AXI input
     */
    input  wire [DATA_WIDTH-1:0]  s_axis_tdata,
    input  wire [KEEP_WIDTH-1:0]  s_axis_tkeep,
    input  wire                   s_axis_tvalid,
    output wire                   s_axis_tready,
    input  wire                   s_axis_tlast,
    input  wire [ID_WIDTH-1:0]    s_axis_tid,
    input  wire [DEST_WIDTH-1:0]  s_axis_tdest,
    input  wire [USER_WIDTH-1:0]  s_axis_tuser,

    /*
     * AXI output
     */
    output wire                   m_axis_hdr_valid,
    input  wire                   m_axis_hdr_ready,
    output wire                   m_axis_hdr_pad,
    output wire                   m_axis_hdr_truncate,
    output wire [15:0]            m_axis_hdr_length,
    output wire [15:0]            m_axis_hdr_original_length,
    output wire [DATA_WIDTH-1:0]  m_axis_tdata,
    output wire [KEEP_WIDTH-1:0]  m_axis_tkeep,
    output wire                   m_axis_tvalid,
    input  wire                   m_axis_tready,
    output wire                   m_axis_tlast,
    output wire [ID_WIDTH-1:0]    m_axis_tid,
    output wire [DEST_WIDTH-1:0]  m_axis_tdest,
    output wire [USER_WIDTH-1:0]  m_axis_tuser,

    /*
     * Configuration
     */
    input  wire [15:0]            length_min,
    input  wire [15:0]            length_max
);

wire [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] fifo_axis_tdata;
wire [KEEP_WIDTH-1:0] fifo_axis_tkeep;
wire fifo_axis_tvalid;
wire fifo_axis_tready;
wire fifo_axis_tlast;
wire [ID_WIDTH-1:0] fifo_axis_tid;
wire [DEST_WIDTH-1:0] fifo_axis_tdest;
wire [USER_WIDTH-1:0] fifo_axis_tuser;

wire status_valid;
wire status_ready;
wire status_frame_pad;
wire status_frame_truncate;
wire [15:0] status_frame_length;
wire [15:0] status_frame_original_length;

axis_frame_length_adjust #(
    .DATA_WIDTH(DATA_WIDTH),
    .KEEP_ENABLE(KEEP_ENABLE),
    .KEEP_WIDTH(KEEP_WIDTH),
    .ID_ENABLE(ID_ENABLE),
    .ID_WIDTH(ID_WIDTH),
    .DEST_ENABLE(DEST_ENABLE),
    .DEST_WIDTH(DEST_WIDTH),
    .USER_ENABLE(USER_ENABLE),
    .USER_WIDTH(USER_WIDTH)
)
axis_frame_length_adjust_inst (
    .clk(clk),
    .rst(rst),
    // AXI input
    .s_axis_tdata(s_axis_tdata),
    .s_axis_tkeep(s_axis_tkeep),
    .s_axis_tvalid(s_axis_tvalid),
    .s_axis_tready(s_axis_tready),
    .s_axis_tlast(s_axis_tlast),
    .s_axis_tid(s_axis_tid),
    .s_axis_tdest(s_axis_tdest),
    .s_axis_tuser(s_axis_tuser),
    // AXI output
    .m_axis_tdata(fifo_axis_tdata),
    .m_axis_tkeep(fifo_axis_tkeep),
    .m_axis_tvalid(fifo_axis_tvalid),
    .m_axis_tready(fifo_axis_tready),
    .m_axis_tlast(fifo_axis_tlast),
    .m_axis_tid(fifo_axis_tid),
    .m_axis_tdest(fifo_axis_tdest),
    .m_axis_tuser(fifo_axis_tuser),
    // Status
    .status_valid(status_valid),
    .status_ready(status_ready),
    .status_frame_pad(status_frame_pad),
    .status_frame_truncate(status_frame_truncate),
    .status_frame_length(status_frame_length),
    .status_frame_original_length(status_frame_original_length),
    // Configuration
    .length_min(length_min),
    .length_max(length_max)
);

axis_fifo #(
    .DEPTH(FRAME_FIFO_DEPTH),
    .DATA_WIDTH(DATA_WIDTH),
    .KEEP_ENABLE(KEEP_ENABLE),
    .KEEP_WIDTH(KEEP_WIDTH),
    .LAST_ENABLE(1),
    .ID_ENABLE(ID_ENABLE),
    .ID_WIDTH(ID_WIDTH),
    .DEST_ENABLE(DEST_ENABLE),
    .DEST_WIDTH(DEST_WIDTH),
    .USER_ENABLE(USER_ENABLE),
    .USER_WIDTH(USER_WIDTH),
    .FRAME_FIFO(0)
)
frame_fifo_inst (
    .clk(clk),
    .rst(rst),
    // AXI input
    .s_axis_tdata(fifo_axis_tdata),
    .s_axis_tkeep(fifo_axis_tkeep),
    .s_axis_tvalid(fifo_axis_tvalid),
    .s_axis_tready(fifo_axis_tready),
    .s_axis_tlast(fifo_axis_tlast),
    .s_axis_tid(fifo_axis_tid),
    .s_axis_tdest(fifo_axis_tdest),
    .s_axis_tuser(fifo_axis_tuser),
    // AXI output
    .m_axis_tdata(m_axis_tdata),
    .m_axis_tkeep(m_axis_tkeep),
    .m_axis_tvalid(m_axis_tvalid),
    .m_axis_tready(m_axis_tready),
    .m_axis_tlast(m_axis_tlast),
    .m_axis_tid(m_axis_tid),
    .m_axis_tdest(m_axis_tdest),
    .m_axis_tuser(m_axis_tuser),
    // Status
    .status_overflow(),
    .status_bad_frame(),
    .status_good_frame()
);

axis_fifo #(
    .DEPTH(HEADER_FIFO_DEPTH),
    .DATA_WIDTH(1+1+16+16),
    .KEEP_ENABLE(0),
    .LAST_ENABLE(0),
    .ID_ENABLE(0),
    .DEST_ENABLE(0),
    .USER_ENABLE(0),
    .FRAME_FIFO(0)
)
header_fifo_inst (
    .clk(clk),
    .rst(rst),
    // AXI input
    .s_axis_tdata({status_frame_pad, status_frame_truncate, status_frame_length, status_frame_original_length}),
    .s_axis_tkeep(0),
    .s_axis_tvalid(status_valid),
    .s_axis_tready(status_ready),
    .s_axis_tlast(0),
    .s_axis_tid(0),
    .s_axis_tdest(0),
    .s_axis_tuser(0),
    // AXI output
    .m_axis_tdata({m_axis_hdr_pad, m_axis_hdr_truncate, m_axis_hdr_length, m_axis_hdr_original_length}),
    .m_axis_tkeep(),
    .m_axis_tvalid(m_axis_hdr_valid),
    .m_axis_tready(m_axis_hdr_ready),
    .m_axis_tlast(),
    .m_axis_tid(),
    .m_axis_tdest(),
    .m_axis_tuser(),
    // Status
    .status_overflow(),
    .status_bad_frame(),
    .status_good_frame()
);

endmodule

`resetall
rtl.task_top_v3.sv:
`timescale 1ns/1ps
module frame_task(
input wire clk, rst,
input wire [7:0] s_data,
input wire s_valid, s_last,
output wire s_ready,
output wire [7:0] m_data,
output wire m_valid, m_last,
input wire m_ready,
output wire h_valid, h_pad, h_truncate,
output wire [15:0] h_length, h_original_length,
input wire h_ready);

axis_frame_length_adjust_fifo #(
    .DATA_WIDTH(8), .KEEP_ENABLE(0), .KEEP_WIDTH(1),
    .ID_ENABLE(0), .DEST_ENABLE(0), .USER_ENABLE(0),
    .FRAME_FIFO_DEPTH(32), .HEADER_FIFO_DEPTH(8)
) dut (
    .clk(clk), .rst(rst),
    .s_axis_tdata(s_data), .s_axis_tkeep(1'b1),
    .s_axis_tvalid(s_valid), .s_axis_tready(s_ready), .s_axis_tlast(s_last),
    .s_axis_tid(8'd0), .s_axis_tdest(8'd0), .s_axis_tuser(1'b0),
    .m_axis_tdata(m_data), .m_axis_tkeep(),
    .m_axis_tvalid(m_valid), .m_axis_tready(m_ready), .m_axis_tlast(m_last),
    .m_axis_tid(), .m_axis_tdest(), .m_axis_tuser(),
    .m_axis_hdr_valid(h_valid), .m_axis_hdr_ready(h_ready),
    .m_axis_hdr_pad(h_pad), .m_axis_hdr_truncate(h_truncate),
    .m_axis_hdr_length(h_length), .m_axis_hdr_original_length(h_original_length),
    .length_min(16'd4), .length_max(16'd8)
);
endmodule

specification:
# Byte-stream length adjustment controller: fixed project contract v1

This task uses the unmodified MIT-licensed verilog-axis length-adjustment FIFO controller
at revision 48ff7a7e2ef782cf778d47910cf85835c64b1bce. It is a newly scoped
monitor task on a previously inspected IP family, not an unseen repository or
an official benchmark. The upstream README describes padding/truncation and
original/current length reports; the timing and finite-trace rules below are
the explicit project contract, not a claim of verbatim upstream prose.

The selected wrapper is task_top_v3.sv. Original data/header FIFOs have depths32/8; status can be consumed before the corresponding output frame. The rejected direct-core scope and its status-stability counterexample remain separate qualification evidence. Data width is 8 bits, KEEP is disabled
(each accepted input is exactly one byte), ID/DEST/USER are disabled. Length
limits are constant MIN=4 and MAX=8 bytes. Input frames contain 1..12 bytes.
There is one positive-edge clock and synchronous active-high reset. Reset is
the only cancellation mechanism in this scope; there is no independent cancel pin.

A transfer occurs at a rising edge iff valid and ready are both 1 before that
edge and rst=0. Input s_last marks the final byte of an input frame. The source
holds s_valid, s_data and s_last while blocked, except that reset cancels it.
Input gaps, back-to-back frames and independent data/status backpressure are
legal. Source validity during reset is 0. The sink need not keep ready asserted.

For each accepted input frame X of length L, the expected output frame is:

- L<4: all input bytes, then zero bytes until length 4;
- 4<=L<=8: the input bytes unchanged;
- L>8: the first 8 bytes; the remaining input bytes are still accepted/drained.

Exactly one accepted output beat has m_last=1 per completed output frame, on
its final byte. Frames and bytes retain input order. No output may depend on
an unaccepted input byte. Output may stream before input s_last is accepted;
the checker must support partial known prefixes rather than requiring the
whole input frame to arrive first. Padding is known only after input completion.
For truncation the output end may wait for the rest of the input frame.

Each completed, uncancelled input frame has exactly one status response:
h_original_length=L, h_length=min(max(L,4),8), h_pad=(L<4), h_truncate=(L>8).
Statuses preserve input-frame order. Data and status responses are independent
channels; no required order is imposed between the two channels' completion.
A status cannot describe an input frame before that input frame completes.

If m_valid=1 and m_ready=0, m_valid/data/last remain stable until transfer or
reset. If h_valid=1 and h_ready=0, h_valid and all status fields remain stable
until transfer or reset. Payload fields when their valid is 0 are unspecified.
s_ready is flow control, not an independently prescribed cycle-by-cycle value.

Reset cancels in-progress input and all not-yet-consumed data/status responses.
After the reset edge m_valid=h_valid=0. Already consumed output prefixes are
not retroactively failures: reset discards the remaining epoch. No pre-reset
obligation may be carried into the next epoch. A reset edge performs no transfer.
Pre-edge observations while rst=1 may still show pre-reset values.

This is a two-state task. Saved -1 observations denote X/Z and are unresolved
when meaningful, never successful checks. The initial pre sample is excluded.
At every subsequent pre/post sample, valid fields and enabled payloads are checked.
Unknowns must not erase an earlier definite violation.

Finite evaluation traces declare require_drained=true and end in an uninterrupted
ready-high, reset-low, no-new-offer tail of at least 32 cycles (development) or
128 cycles (final). For the fixed bounded offered workload, all offered bytes
must be accepted and all uncancelled responses consumed by the end. Remaining
s_valid/m_valid/h_valid, an incomplete accepted input frame or remaining expected
responses is a finite completion failure, not permission to infer an unbounded
liveness guarantee. Partial unit controls may use require_drained=false.

## Sampling clarification v2

This registered FIFO task has no zero-latency pre-edge bypass. At pre(n), valid payload/status must be justified by inputs accepted at earlier edges; a current input offer does not justify a pre-edge output. At post(n), the input accepted at edge n is included. A presented m_valid or h_valid without the requisite already accepted input/frame is a specification failure even if ready=0 and even if a later reset cancels it. Reset cannot erase an earlier violation.

Source protocol violations (valid during reset or changing a blocked offer) are INVALID_INPUT, as are malformed observations. This is input classification, not a DUT pass. Final evaluation explicitly uses min_tail=128; development uses min_tail=32. Insufficient tails are UNRESOLVED, never PASS.
